milestone.title: mp watch --resume — crash and SIGINT recovery

intent.outcome: If mp watch is interrupted (crash, SIGINT, closed laptop), re-running it detects the in-flight milestone and any live herdr panes and re-attaches instead of re-spawning duplicate agents or losing track of progress.

problem.description: M149's scope lists graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown (marking in-flight milestones) but not resumption. The whole value proposition of mp watch is 'walk away' — but a single interrupted run that cannot resume forces the user back to manual lifecycle driving, defeating the purpose. Re-attaching to existing herdr panes (herdr agent attach, herdr agent list) and reconciling against plan.json lifecycle is the operability gap that makes mp watch production-grade.

in_scope: On startup, query herdr agent list for existing role-runner-N / role-coordinator-N panes and reconcile against the target milestone's lifecycle
mp watch --resume re-attaches to live panes; mp watch (default) refuses to double-spawn if a pane already exists for the role, unless --force
Crash-safe watch state file (.mp/watch.state.json) recording the active milestone, pane ids, and last-known lifecycle
Tests for resume-after-sigint and pane-already-exists detection
out_of_scope: Re-driving a milestone whose lifecycle already advanced past the interrupted stage (skip cleanly instead)

design_decisions.choice: watch.state.json is operational scratch; plan.json lifecycle remains authoritative for milestone state
design_decisions.rationale: The state file only tracks pane ids and pid for re-attachment. Milestone progress is always re-derived from plan.json on resume so a stale or deleted state file never corrupts plan truth.

design_decisions.choice: default refuses to double-spawn; --force opts in
design_decisions.rationale: Two runner panes on one milestone cause duplicate work and conflicting plan writes. Refusing by default protects the unwary; --force is the explicit override for the confident operator.

findings.description: F-01 — upsert_panes_from_cache overwrites spawned_at and drops last_status (crates/mp/src/commands/watch.rs:556-580, called at lines 326 and 372). The state file's pane entries lose their original spawn timestamp and any observed agent-status: every re-upsert writes `spawned_at: now_rfc3339()` and `last_status: None`, regardless of what was there before. Real impact: a user reviewing watch.state.json after a crash cannot tell when a pane was first spawned or what status it had last. Forensic value of the state file degrades on every re-save. Fix: PaneHandle (in watch/herdr.rs) should carry the original spawned_at and last_status, and upsert_panes_from_cache should preserve them when populating the state. Alternatively, extend PaneState with a "do not overwrite these fields" semantic.
findings.author: external-review(M152)

findings.description: F-02 — graceful_shutdown hardcodes target_lifecycle="self-reviewed" (crates/mp/src/commands/watch.rs:387-392). The shutdown path persists the in-flight milestone with `target_lifecycle: "self-reviewed"` regardless of where the milestone actually was. If the milestone was interrupted at lifecycle=reviewed (waiting for target=Complete via the Approve prompt), the persisted state claims target="self-reviewed" — a lie. On --resume, the state machine uses this to short-circuit plan.json reads; a wrong target means the resume path may bail early or not at the right lifecycle. Fix: persist the actual target the sequencer was waiting for (thread the StagePlan through to shutdown), or omit target_lifecycle when the source isn't known.
findings.author: external-review(M152)

findings.description: F-03 — WatchState::load_from writes warnings via eprintln! (crates/mp/src/watch/state.rs:194-212). Library code writing to stderr directly is a layering smell: the caller might be in a context where stderr is not appropriate (JSON output mode, log capture, daemon mode), and the warning has no structured envelope (severity, milestone, path metadata). Real impact: repeated `mp watch --resume` runs against a corrupt state file spam stderr with `warning: ignoring unreadable watch state ...`. Tests that pipe stderr see the warning pollute their combined-stdout-stderr assertions. Fix: route through `tracing::warn!` (or surface as a struct member on the result) so the caller controls logging.
findings.author: external-review(M152)

findings.description: F-04 — --force semantic vs. behavior mismatch (crates/mp/src/commands/watch.rs:267-339, cli help at crates/mp/src/cli/mod.rs:268-275). The CLI help says `--force` "opts in to ignoring that check" — the gate. But the implementation reuses the existing panes after the gate is bypassed (same as --resume), pre-populating ops.pane_cache from the reconciliation result. A user choosing --force likely expects fresh pane spawns (the flag's name suggests overriding). Real impact: users running `mp watch --force` to recover from a stuck pane get the same pane re-attached, not a fresh one. Fix: either (a) update the help text + AC-03 docs to clarify "--force: bypass gate, then reuse like --resume", or (b) implement --force as "bypass gate, kill existing panes, spawn fresh". The current code silently does (a) while the docs imply (b).
findings.author: external-review(M152)

findings.description: F-05 — WatchState::path instance method is unused dead code (crates/mp/src/watch/state.rs:165-174). The method `pub fn path(&self, plan_dir: &Path) -> PathBuf { Self::path_for(plan_dir) }` exists but is never called anywhere in the codebase. The canonical accessor is `WatchState::path_for`. The instance method just adds a duplicate API surface. Fix: delete the instance method, or if it's intended for downstream consumers, document why it exists and where it's used.
findings.author: external-review(M152)

findings.description: F-06 — build_initial_state ignores _ctx and _ops parameters (crates/mp/src/commands/watch.rs:550-555). The function is just a thin wrapper around `WatchState::fresh(ids)` with two params marked `_ctx` and `_ops` that are never used. Real impact: the function signature implies it does more than it does, which makes grep-based reasoning harder and encourages future maintainers to "fix" the unused params by adding logic that drifts from the simple shape. Fix: either inline the call (`WatchState::fresh(ids)` directly at the call site) or remove the unused params.
findings.author: external-review(M152)
